packs.title: Museums, Parks and Lake
packs.promise: Explore Rochester's play, image-making, gardens, river parks and Lake Ontario across separate outings.

q.s: Record what one Eastman Museum photograph shows and what it cannot establish.
st: Select one photograph from an open gallery or official collection record.
Describe a visible composition detail and record the museum credit separately.
Write one thing the image alone does not prove about its subject.

q.s: Make a seasonal plant map without depending on spring lilacs.
st: Use an open park path or the County's plant map.
Sketch two different planted areas or specimen forms.
Mark one feature whose appearance changes by season rather than promising a bloom.

q.t: Where the City Meets the Lake
q.s: Record a Lake Ontario shoreline view from Ontario Beach Park.
st: Find a public sand or promenade viewpoint, or use the County park image.
Describe one shoreline form and one human-made feature.
Note separately which seasonal facility is optional rather than required.

packs.title: High Falls to Center City
packs.promise: Follow connected river, preservation, art and civic stops in two afternoon walks.

q.s: Trace how an old road bridge became a public pedestrian crossing.
st: Observe the bridge's truss from its open pedestrian deck or City image.
Identify one structural feature and the two sides it connects.
Record a safe crossing plan, naming the former vehicle use separately from today's pedestrian use.

q.s: Draw how Austin Steward Plaza links public paths and a commemorated name.
st: Find the plaza's river-flow pattern or the City's plan image.
Sketch one connection between the river path and a downtown street.
Add one City-sourced line explaining whom the plaza commemorates.

q.s: Observe how Washington Square serves reflection and everyday rest.
st: Find the Lincoln monument from a public path or the City's park page.
Describe one feature of the memorial and one ordinary park use.
Keep today's observation distinct from the City's event examples.
